routes.name: Ruth-Icy Traverse (Northwest Ridge, via Ruth Mountain)

claims.says: a long ~12-13 hr day two

contradictions.why: The day-2 schedule runs 4:00 AM to 4:30 PM (12.5 hr) and the totalNote says 12-13 hr, but the day's hours and the timing breakdown say 10.5.
contradictions.internal_resolution: Schedule and totalNote agree on ~12.5 hr; the 10.5 figure (and timing.totalHrs 16) is the outlier.

contradictions.fact: Height lost/regained between Ruth and the Ruth-Icy saddle

claims.says: descend Ruth's south/west side about 800 ft ... down to the Ruth–Icy saddle (~5,700 ft)
Ruth Mountain's summit (7,115 ft)
roughly 2,000 ft of regain back up to Ruth Mountain's summit/camp
Roughly 2,000 ft of regain over Ruth on the way home
~5,700 ft; about a 900-ft drop from camp

contradictions.why: Ruth 7,115 ft to a 5,700 ft saddle is ~1,400 ft, not 'about 800 ft', and the regain is quoted as ~2,000 ft (or 900 ft from the 6,600 ft notch camp).
contradictions.internal_resolution: Elevations (7,115 summit, 6,600 camp, 5,700 saddle) imply ~1,400 ft from the summit / ~900 ft from camp; the 800 ft and 2,000 ft figures are both off.

claims.says: parties report ~12 hours car-to-car when done in a single push
very strong parties occasionally link it car-to-car in one long (15-20 hr) day instead

contradictions.why: Two different durations for the same one-day push.

claims.says: After 6:00 PM
Hike out to trailhead

contradictions.why: 15.5 hr from a 1:45 AM wake ends ~5:15 PM, yet the schedule only starts the ~7-mile hike out after 6 PM, implying a ~19-20 hr day.

claims.says: Some approaches cross into North Cascades National Park land on the upper mountain, where a free NPS backcountry permit is required
Mount Baker Wilderness, with some upper routes crossing into North Cascades National Park
This is national forest, not national park, so no park backcountry permit applies and none can be obtained for it
Mount Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest (Mount Baker Wilderness)

contradictions.why: Boilerplate says the route may enter the national park and need an NPS permit; the camp entry says the area is national forest only.
contradictions.internal_resolution: landManager and the bivy permit agree it is Mount Baker Wilderness only; the NCNP clause is generic boilerplate.

claims.says: Free self-issue Mount Baker Wilderness permit or trailhead registration
No wilderness permit required; free self-issue permits available at the trailhead.
No overnight wilderness permit is required and none is issued for this area

contradictions.why: One field offers a free self-issue wilderness permit; the camp entry says none is issued.

claims.says: The standard and only remotely feasible route on Lincoln Peak.
it was the only documented route to the summit until a 2015 first ascent opened a second line on the NW Face

contradictions.why: Beta calls this the only feasible route while the overview documents a second established route.
contradictions.internal_resolution: The overview (and the sibling Wilkes-Booth row) show a second route exists; the beta wording is stale.

contradictions.fact: Glacier crossed to reach the face

claims.says: From Heliotrope Ridge, cross the lower Thunder Glacier to the base of Lincoln's northwest face
Glacier gear for the approach across the Thunder Glacier.
If you find yourself descending toward a cirque with no icefall above you, you have cut left toward the Thunder Glacier side and are heading for the southwest face.
Cross the Coleman Glacier approach into the amphitheater between Lincoln Peak and Assassin Spire.
Coleman Glacier toe / rope-up point

contradictions.why: The approach and pro_needs send the party across the Thunder Glacier, while the approach variant says Thunder Glacier is the wrong side and the itinerary and waypoints use the Coleman.
contradictions.internal_resolution: Approach variant, itinerary, waypoints (Coleman toe, Black Buttes basin camp) and watch_out all use the Coleman; the Thunder Glacier mentions in approach and pro_needs are the outliers.

contradictions.why: The summit pin sits 5.2 mi out (≈10.4 mi round trip), the header shows 14 mi, and TECHNICAL STATS shows 9 km (5.6 mi).

before the technical ridge climbing begins

contradictions.internal_resolution: Overview, beta, pitch_detail and face all describe a NW-face WI4 ice route; the 'ridge' text is left over from the old north_ridge record.

claims.says: drops roughly 900 ft into the Lake Ann basin before climbing back out
drops about 700 ft into the Swift Creek headwaters basin

The upper highway to Austin Pass typically isn't snow-free and open until around July

claims.says: Aim to be off the glacier by mid-morning before the snow turns to slush.

claims.says: a long (10-14 hr) technical summit day

glacier travel

claims.says: Early-mid afternoon
Evening

claims.says: Jul-Aug

marginal

claims.says: roughly 16 miles and 8,100 ft round trip
8,000 ft of gain from the lowest trailhead on the peak

contradictions.why: The header gain of 7,000 ft is below even the net rise from a 2,700 ft trailhead to the 10,781 ft summit (8,081 ft); the itinerary and variant say ~8,000-8,100.

claims.says: Boulder Ridge trailhead to camp at the toe of the Cleaver

at roughly 5,500 to 5,700 ft just below the Boulder Glacier
